The hike begins with a walk along the beach. You will then climb for about an hour to an elevation of 350 metres.

There will be stops at viewpoints along the way, including Pedra da Bigorna. From here you can see wild beaches, Rio, neighbouring cliffs and the sandy spit of Restinga da Marambaia.

At the summit stands the famous rock ledge of Pedra do Telégrafo, where travellers often stop for a photo session. The views are especially striking at sunset.

Get ready for an exciting day trip combining history, culture and extraordinary natural beauty!

## Discovering El Peñol's Past: Climbing the Rock and Exploring Guatapé

Your adventure begins with a convenient hotel pickup at 9:00 AM. Step into history: travel to the municipality of El Peñol and explore its distinctive architectural heritage. Visit the replica of the original town, a reminder of the region's colonial past, and admire its charming style. You will hear the fascinating story of how the original town was flooded to create an important reservoir. Marvel at the majestic Piedra del Peñol, a towering 220-metre monolith. Climb its 740 steps, a memorable ascent rewarded with breathtaking panoramas of the surrounding landscape.

## Exploring the Colours of Guatapé

A town unlike any other: explore colourful Guatapé, known for its vibrant atmosphere and distinctive architecture. Discover the elaborate zócalos, colourful baseboards decorated with designs and relief images that adorn the town's houses. A symphony of colour: admire the blend of bright shades and intricate patterns. Immerse yourself in nature's beauty: visit the spectacular Peñol and Guatapé reservoirs, where calm waters reflect green mountains, creating a remarkable natural contrast. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere and take memorable photographs.

A full-day excursion to Perito Moreno Glacier with a Russian-speaking guide, including admission to Los Glaciares National Park and a boat safari (in a shared group) right beside the ice front.
Perito Moreno is one of the few glaciers in the world that continues to advance rather than retreat. Wooden walkways offer breathtaking views of its 5-kilometre ice front, rising up to 74 metres above the waters of Lake Argentino.

Perito Moreno descends from the Andes towards Lake Argentino. Tall ridges, crevasses and different shades of blue are clearly visible in its ice wall. From the viewpoints, you can watch the water moving at the foot of the glacier.

Large pieces of ice sometimes break away from its edge. They crash into the lake with a roar and send waves across the water. The timing of such an event cannot be predicted, so the excursion focuses on the glacier itself and the surrounding scenery.

The group is accompanied by an English-speaking guide. Walking on the ice and a boat safari are not included in this excursion module.
